{{nihongo|'''Ooba Shrine'''|大庭神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Sagami Province]].

== Oba Shrine (Inari, Fujisawa City) ==
'''Oba Shrine'' is located near the border with {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|Q127513|qid=Q127513}}{{ill|Fujisawa, Kanagawa|ar|فوجيساوا (كاناغاوا)|arz|فوجيساوا|azb|فوجیساوا، کاناقاوا|be|Фудзісава|bg|Фуджисава|ca|Fujisawa|ce|Фудзисава (гӀала)|ceb|Fujisawa|cs|Fudžisawa (Kanagawa)|de|Fujisawa (Kanagawa)|eo|Fuĝisava|es|Fujisawa|et|Fujisawa|eu|Fujisawa (Kanagawa)|fa|فوجیساوا، کاناگاوا|fi|Fujisawa|fr|Fujisawa|gl|Fujisawa, Kanagawa|hy|Ֆուձիսավա|it|Fujisawa|ja|藤沢市|ko|후지사와시|lt|Fudžisava|mg|Fujisawa|mzn|فوجیساوا، کاناگاوا|nl|Fujisawa|no|Fujisawa|pl|Fujisawa|pt|Fujisawa|ro|Fujisawa|ru|Фудзисава (город)|sh|Fujisava, Kanagava|simple|Fujisawa, Kanagawa|sr|Фуџисава (Канагава)|sv|Fujisawa|szl|Fujisawa|tg|Фуҷисава|th|ฟูจิซาวะ (จังหวัดคานางาวะ)|tl|Fujisawa, Kanagawa|tr|Fujisawa|tt|Фудзисава (шәһәр)|uk|Фудзісава (Канаґава)|ur|فوجیساوا، کاناگاوا|uz|Fujisawa (Kanagawa)|vi|Fujisawa, Kanagawa|war|Fujisawa, Kanagawa|zh|藤澤市|zh_classical|藤澤市|zh_min_nan|Huzisawa-chhī|zh_yue|藤澤|qid=Q386661}} Inari <ref group="notes">{{ill|Ōba|ja|大庭 (藤沢市)|qid=Q11435364|lt=Oba}}. It is {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} that is enshrined in </ref>. Located on {{ill|Hügelland|Q222912|qid=Q222912}} along {{ill|Hikiji River|arz|نهر هيكيجى|fa|رود هیکیجی|ja|引地川|qid=Q11487144}}. In the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, it was called "Tenjingu," "Oba Daimyojin," and "Oba Tenmangu." Oba Shrine] (Investigation of Engishiki Shrine)</ref>.

== History ==
Although "Engishiki Jinmyocho" compiled in the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}} mentions "{{ill|Kōza District, Kanagawa|ar|مقاطعة كوزا (كاناغاوا)|ceb|Kōza-gun|de|Kōza-gun|fr|District de Kōza|it|Distretto di Kōza|ja|高座郡|ko|고자군|pl|Powiat Kōza|th|อำเภอโคซะ|uk|Повіт Кодза|zh|高座郡|qid=Q1202776}} Oba Shrine," there are no other records (shaden) prior to {{ill|Early modern period|Q5308718|qid=Q5308718}}. The information board in the precincts about our company's history says, ``It was ranked as one of the 13 Sagami shrines and is a small shrine, and this place has been passed down as an old place since ancient times.'' "Sagami 13-no-Ichi Nishite-kosha 2 rows of Serarere are the old folklore of ancient places"</ref>.

The {{ill|Bonshō|ar|بونشو|bn|বোনশো|de|Bonshō|es|Bonshō|fa|بونشو|fr|Bonshō|id|Bonshō|ja|梵鐘|ko|범종|pl|Japońskie dzwony, dzwonki i gongi|pt|Bonshō|ru|Бонсё|th|บนโช|zh|佛鐘|qid=Q8192099}} in the temple grounds was built in {{ill|Kyōhō|de|Kyōhō|es|Kyōhō|fa|کیوهو|fr|Ère Kyōhō|ja|享保|ko|교호|ru|Кёхо|simple|Kyōhō|sr|Кјохо|sv|Kyōhō|tr|Kyōhō|zh|享保|qid=Q1145048}}6 ({{ill|1721|Q6913|qid=Q6913}}). alink|casting|Q496098}}, and it is said that the words ``Tenmatenjingu'' were originally written on it, but these words were scratched off and the words ``Oba Daimyojin'' were carved into it. Also, according to "Fujisawa Cultural Properties" published by the {{ill|Board of education|Q399541|qid=Q399541}} of Fujisawa City, our company was called "Tenjin Shrine" before {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}<ref name="shonan-mark">[http://pub.ne.jp/karihomaru/?entry_id=3609822 Two Oba Shrines] (Shonan Mark's room)</ref>.{{ill|An'ei|Q1193910|qid=Q1193910|lt=Yasunaga}}6 ({{ill|1777|Q7709|qid=Q7709}}), King Shien of Jingi acquired Saburo Kagechika Oba, who was based in {{ill|Oba Castle|Q11435376|qid=Q11435376}}, and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tenmei}}3 ({{ill|1783|Q7745|qid=Q7745}}), Michima Sugawara was {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=enshrined}} ({{ill|Co-Enshrinement|Q11412524|qid=Q11412524}}) according to the wishes of Suwabe Sadaro, Yamazaki Rokurobei Kanataka, and others. Before the Meiji era {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ordinance on the Separation of Shinto and Buddhism}}, {{ill|Jōjuin|Q18337056|qid=Q18337056|lt=Jōjuin}}, located behind our company, was managing our company as {{ill|Bettō-ji|ja|別当寺|qid=Q11396755}}<ref name="chosa1" />.

== Transportation ==
{{osm box|n|1229000716|Oba Shrine (Inari, Fujisawa City)}}
* From {{ill|Fujisawa Station|Q1133110|qid=Q1133110}} North Exit/{{ill|Shōnandai Station|Q1036357|qid=Q1036357}} West Exit {{ill|Kanagawa Chuo Kotsu|Q10854960|qid=Q10854960|lt=Kanachu Bus}}{{ill|Fuji 34|Q11588895|qid=Q11588895|lt=Fuji 34}}, or from the west exit of Zengyo Station, take the Kanachu bus {{ill|Zen 03|Q11588895|qid=Q11588895|lt=Zen 03}}, get off at Tenjinsha-mae, and walk 6 minutes to Ichi-no-Torii.
* About 25 minutes walk from Odakyu Line {{ill|Zengyō Station|Q4160904|qid=Q4160904}}.

``Kumano Shrine'' is a shrine located in Fujisawa City, Kanagawa Prefecture {{ill|Ōba|ja|大庭 (藤沢市)|qid=Q11435364|lt=Oba}}. In the Edo period, it was called ``Goryosha'' and ``Gongensha,'' but stone monuments and information boards in the precincts say ``Oba Shrine 舊达''. </ref>, or "Oba Shrine Historic Site" <ref name="chosa2">[https://web.archive.org/web/20151130003000/http://www.geocities.jp/engisiki/sagami/bun/sag160501-02.html Kumano Shrine] (Survey of Engishiki Shrines)</ref>.

== Enshrined God ==
* '''Kumano Kusuhime'''

== Historic site of Oba Shrine and Obago ==
This area is said to be the historic site of Oba Shrine. From the hilly area in front of this area, you can see {{ill|Earthenware|Q1377111|qid=Q1377111}} from the early {{ill|Jōmon period|Q52824|qid=Q52824}} period, {{ill|Yayoi period|Q207858|qid=Q207858}}, and {{jalin} k|Nara Period|Q189178}} Remains of residences have been found ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Oba Tsukiyama Ruins}}), and it is assumed that the {{ill|Human settlement|Q486972|qid=Q486972}} of Oba-go was formed from ancient times.<ref name="chosa2" />.

== History ==
Similar to Oba Shrine, an Inari shrine in the same city (see {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=previous section}}), there are no records (shrine biographies) from before modern times.

It was during the Edo period that our company became the historic site of Oba Shrine (Oba Shrine). name="chosa2" />. The aforementioned ``Fujisawa Cultural Properties'' discusses that our company was originally ``Oba Shrine,'' an Engishiki shrine, but that for some reason, Oba Shrine in Inari came to be regarded as an Engishiki shrine <ref name="shonan-mark" />.

On the other hand, it is also said that it was {{ill|Bunrei|Q195793|qid=Q195793}} ({{ill|Bunsha|Q18989808|qid=Q18989808}}) from {{ill|Goryō Shrine (Miyamae, Fujisawa)|Q20044399|qid=Q20044399|lt=Goryo Shrine}} located in Miyamae, Fujisawa City.

In {{ill|Tenpō|Q1369045|qid=Q1369045}}4 ({{ill|1833|Q7587|qid=Q7587}}), a stone torii gate was donated by Rokubei Masahiko Yamazaki. Furthermore, this shrine was also managed by Joju-in until the Meiji era's ordinance separating Shinto and Buddhism<ref name="chosa2" />.
